newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Frankfurt and London stocks hit new highs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Frankfurt and London stocks hit new highs.

text.p: Leading German and British stocks hit fresh highs on Monday, boosted by Wall Street's strong close last week as the U.S. market celebrated positive inflation data.

The German DAX index closed bourse trade at a record, underpinned by the firmer dollar, which makes German exports more attractive. The index ended up 33.91 points at 2,629.87 from a session high 2,630.32, 1.3 percent -- about 30 points -- above its previous intra-day peak, set on Friday.

London stocks firmed to about eight points up on their Friday record high, but off their Monday opening peak of 3,980.8, after Wall Street opened firmer. Dealers said cautious investors were still sitting back to see if New York could repeat its 1.15 percent rise of Friday, when the Dow closed at a record 5,838.52 as treasuries powered ahead.

"It was a very predictable move. We saw a squeeze up on the opening after Friday's euphoria and then it came back. It feels like it will still go to 4,000 this week but we will have to have Wall Street very strong to get it there," said one trader.
Dealers were sceptical whether the psychological 4,000 level could be passed on Monday, despite talk that investment funds were poised to pump more cash into the market.

"I think we would have to wait for more significant corporate news before that comes. Volumes weren't that exciting on Friday. Also, there are some suspicions about whether Wall Street can hold those gains," one said.

The Paris bourse moved higher, extending last week's 3.77 percent advance, helped by the stronger opening on Wall Street. The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 10.22 points, or half a percent at 1430 GMT.

On the Milan bourse, Olivetti shares were automatically suspended after plunging 10 percent following news that the crisis-hit Italian information technology group's chief executive was under preliminary investigation by magistrates.
In foreign exchange, the dollar was stuck in a tight range though slightly firmer than Friday's closing levels. Analysts said there was little likely to stir the market up.
With Tokyo out overnight for a market holiday, early volume was light and traders reckoned there was a good chance the dollar could give up some of its recent gains during the course of the week.
Support lent by the Iraq crisis was fading, they said, and the view was growing that U.S. interest rates would be left unchanged at the September 24 meeting of the Federal Open Markets Committee.

"The dollar is likely to struggle this week to hold on to its recent gains," said Klaus Baader, currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "Most importantly, interest rate support is waning." Buoyant oil prices eased on Monday after Iraq appeared to defuse a military standoff with Washington by suspending attacks on U.S. warplanes patrolling Iraqi no fly zones.

November futures for international benchmark North Sea Brent blend were trading down 68 cents at $22.45 a barrel by mid afternoon in London. Brent for October hit a five-year post Gulf War peak at $24.39 a barrel last Thursday after Iraq fired missiles at U.S. planes and Washington sent more weaponry to the region.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5128 marks and 110.43 yen compared with late Friday's 1.5112 marks and 110.32 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares had risen 10.7 points to 3,978.6.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index gained 8.48 to 2,088.85.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 33.91 at 2,629.87.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $382.80, compared with Friday's London close of $383.10. Silver was down two cents at $5.05.
